content:
In connection with a project to formalize B. C. Carlson's Special Functions of Applied Mathematics (1977) I needed some results on several complex variables and then some results on complex analysis of one variable, beyond what I could find in Mathlib. This grew into a diversion that is now in a GitHub repository lean-CA. I hope that the work will be of broader interest.

Elements of the project include global Cauchy and residue theory, Runge approximation and Mittag-Leffler, normal families and the Riemann mapping theorem, entire-function factorization, and selected parts of univalent-function and potential theory.

For this effort I selected textbook sources for the material to be covered as listed below. (The list expanded as the project progressed.) From there on all development was done in interaction with AI/LLM operating as agents; primarily recent instances of GPT and Claude, and also Grok. General instructions to the AI included to follow Mathlib conventions wherever possible in matters of generality of statements, namespace choices and naming conventions for definitions and theorems. All the Lean proofs were done by AI exclusively.

Source material:

  • [APP] Agarwal, Perera, Pinelas, An Introduction to Complex Analysis (2011), Lectures 25–44.
  • [BN] Bak, Newman, Complex Analysis, 3rd ed. (2010), Chapters 4–18.
  • [Bu] Burckel, Classical Analysis in the Complex Plane (2021), Chapters II–VIII.
  • [C1] Conway, Functions of One Complex Variable I (1978), Chapters IV–XII.
  • [C2] Conway, Functions of One Complex Variable II (1995), Chapters 13–15, 20, 21.
  • [Ga] Gamelin, Complex Analysis (2001), Chapters II–VII.
  • [He] Heins, Complex Function Theory (1968), Chapters IV–VIII.
  • [La] Lang, Complex Analysis, 4th ed. (1999), Chapters I–XIII.
  • [Re] Remmert, Theory of Complex Functions (1991), Chapters 6–8.
  • [Si] Simon, A Comprehensive Course in Analysis, Part 2A (2015), Chapters 2–4.
  • [SS] Stein, Shakarchi, Complex Analysis (2003), Chapters 2–3.

For all these sources except [Si] the LLM agent had access to a PDF. For [Si] I have the hardcopy but the LLM agents only have a PDF of the table of contents.

The file STRUCTURE.md provides a more detailed description of the project organization. It is written for potential future developers.

The file SYNOPSIS.md provides a more detailed description of the mathematical content. It is written for mathematicians.

The file CREDITS.md points to related and sometimes overlapping efforts that were found in the course of the project.

The file Challenge.lean contains 45 theorems from the project, presented here in the manner requested for the Palomar registry, so with a sorry for the proof.

I hope that this will be useful somewhere, and also I will appreciate to hear of any other efforts or developments that might be noted in CREDITS.md.
